# finding-report: crates/tsc-client (2026-09-28, ranger:audit, 99 candidates -> 6 adversary clusters)

Crate: crates/tsc-client (standalone, unconsumed, uncommitted). Contract under audit: Lifecycle gate in docs/type-checker-integration.md ("missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification"). All evidence below was reproduced by adversaries (throwaway tests, fake-tsc, /bin/sh stubs, and the real typescript@next 7.1.0-dev.20260926.1); throwaway files were deleted.

## Family A — a session has no terminal state (structural)
Root cause: `ClientInner` has no closed/terminal state. The reader task drains `pending` exactly once on its natural exit; nothing marks the session closed, `request()` never checks, `shutdown()` aborts the reader before it drains, and `Supervisor::request` decides to restart only from the current call's error (Crashed|Write), never from whether the session's reader ended.
- CONFIRMED medium C006/C013 (client.rs:66,:139,:121): request after reader exit inserts into `pending`, never resolved -> full-deadline `Timeout` naming the wrong cause (garbage_bytes: 3.0037s).
- CONFIRMED medium C011/C054 (supervisor.rs:211 + client.rs:121): `shutdown()` aborts reader, `fail_all_pending` skipped; in-flight request on a Client clone waits its whole deadline (real tsc: shutdown 0.7ms, request 30.0s -> Timeout).
- CONFIRMED medium NEW-1 (supervisor.rs:171): OversizedFrame/MalformedFrame(header)/Read ends the reader while the child stays alive; Supervisor never restarts, storm cap never trips, every later request Timeouts (4/4 at 300ms, is_alive=false, spawns=1). `is_alive()` detects it, nothing calls it.
- CONFIRMED low C-crashed-status (client.rs:118): `Crashed.status` always None; exit status is discarded in restart (supervisor.rs:198) and shutdown (:215).
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C005 (client.rs:54): well-framed but non-JSON/mis-shaped body only warn!-logged, waiter Timeouts; `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson` never constructed.
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C020/C021 (protocol.rs:58,:62): null/non-u64 id or `{"id":1}` with no result dropped -> Timeout; id+method frame misfiled as Notification. Real pinned tsc sends neither (0 notifications observed).
- Doc defect: `Supervisor::client` doc promises `SessionClosed` for stale clones; in practice Write/Crashed/Timeout (SessionClosed effectively unreachable).

## Family B — the write path is not owned by the session (structural)
Root cause: any caller's future performs a multi-poll `write_frame` while holding the shared stdin mutex, and `deadline` wraps only the response `rx`. Also stdin lives inside `ClientInner`, so only dropping every Client clone closes it.
- CONFIRMED high C015/C074 (client.rs:150-158, framing.rs:124): dropping a `Client::request` future mid-write (select!/timeout) leaves a partial frame on the pipe; every later request on every clone then Timeouts, `is_alive()` stays true, no Crashed/Write, never restarted (8 MiB body, echo fake: 3/3 later pings Timeout ~502ms).
- CONFIRMED medium C-stdin-lock-deadline (client.rs:151): child that stops reading stdin -> write blocks past `deadline` holding the mutex; other requests queue behind it (1 MiB/100ms deadline still blocked at 2s; 4 KiB frames: request 15 blocks once the ~64 KiB pipe fills).
- CONFIRMED low C055/C056 (supervisor.rs:212): with any `supervisor.client()` clone held, stdin never closes, so tsc (which exits on stdin EOF: 1.26ms without clone) always takes the 2s grace + SIGKILL (2.003s). Reaping still guaranteed.
- Note: framing.rs module doc claim "a frame is always fully formed before it's sent ... no partial-state problem" is false under cancellation.

## Family C — untrusted child output is not bounded (local fixes)
- PLAUSIBLE medium C061/C059/C069 (framing.rs:51,:93): no header-size cap; no `\r\n\r\n` grows the buffer without bound and rescans from offset 0 each decode (real FramedRead over `yes`: 84 MB in 10.6s; 128 MiB direct decode 42.7s, quadratic). Real pinned tsc emits only `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n` on stdout, so not confirmed.
- PLAUSIBLE medium C030 (supervisor.rs:81): stderr drain `while let Ok(Some(..))` stops on first read error (non-UTF-8 line), drops the pipe, tsc dies of SIGPIPE on next stderr write -> silent crash/restart (reproduced with a stand-in child).
- PLAUSIBLE low C063 (framing.rs:61): header name matched case-sensitively with exactly one space; real tsc emits exactly `Content-Length: %d`.
- PLAUSIBLE low C058 (supervisor.rs:219): on Node without `process.execve` (or Windows) `bin/tsc` falls back to execFileSync -> native tsc becomes a grandchild that start_kill/kill_on_drop do not kill.
- Hardening note C008 (client.rs:96): unbounded notification channel; pinned tsc sent 0 notifications -> dismissed for the pinned build.

## Family D — declared but unenforced contract (mixed)
- CONFIRMED low C-handshake (supervisor.rs:31): `SupervisorConfig.handshake_timeout` (default 10s) is never read; a tsc that starts but never becomes ready is never detected or restarted (spawn Ok in 285us, request Timeouts, no restart). Real nightly answers `initialize` in ms.
- CONFIRMED low C038 (supervisor.rs:128): `failed` is terminal forever; after 3 restarts in 60s (e.g. UnsupportedVersion after `npm i typescript@next`) every call is RestartStormDetected even after the cause is fixed; message says "restarted 3 times" although no restart succeeded and hides the root cause.
- PLAUSIBLE medium C041 (supervisor.rs:173): after restart the request is replayed unchanged into a fresh tsc with no session setup (`{"snapshot":1,"symbol":42}` replayed into process 3 returned Ok); TaggedResponse.seq restarts at 1, so fresh answers compare as stale under `answer.seq > update_ack.seq`. Depends on how real tsc treats per-run IDs.
- Cleanup: `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson` dead variant; `saw_header_line` dead branch in `parse_content_length`; `Ordering::SeqCst` stronger than needed.
- Test gap: `shutdown_force_kills_and_reaps_a_process_that_ignores_it` never reaches the force-kill branch (fake exits on stdin EOF; 107ms) — it only runs when a Client clone is held.

## Dismissed (with evidence; do not re-litigate)
C016 late-response misattribution (ids unique), C057/C031/C029/C033-C035 (start_kill, kill_on_drop, stderr task leak, unreachable! after Stdio::piped), C060/C067 (decoder state after error: reader breaks on first Err, FramedRead returns None), C064/C065 (`+2` and duplicate Content-Length cause no misframing on a one-parser pipe), C072/C073 (partial header at EOF correctly mapped to Crashed), C047/C049-C053 (backoff/cap arithmetic, restart cleanup, old reader isolation), `take_notifications` try_lock (30x16-thread contention: exactly one Some).

## Invisible invariants (no machine enforcement)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable 1 (no `unwrap()` outside #[cfg(test)]): workspace clippy is `all = warn` only; `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` not enabled. tsc-client complies today by convention.
- Non-negotiable 6 (always emit Diagnostic when degrading): convention only; client.rs:54 degrades a bad frame to `warn!` with no signal to the caller.
- crates/core/AGENTS.md panic-containment rule: convention only.

## Family routing
Families A and B share one missing concept: a session that owns its I/O (a writer task that owns stdin and receives whole frames, a reader task, and an explicit closed-with-reason state that request(), shutdown() and the Supervisor all observe). -> scribe:architect. Families C and D are ordinary remediation except C038/C041, which need a small design decision (recovery semantics, replay policy).

The audit is finished, and I've handed the structural findings to the architect.

**What the audit found in `crates/tsc-client`:** 9 confirmed defects, 7 plausible, and about 40 dismissed with evidence. The full report is at `scratchpad/finding-report.md`. Most of it comes from two root causes, both structural:

- **A, a session has no terminal state.** Requests made after the reader dies, and requests in flight during shutdown, wait out their whole deadline and report `Timeout`. A fatal frame error while the child stays alive is never restarted.
- **B, the write path isn't owned by the session.**
  - **Cancellation:** dropping a `request` future mid-write leaves a partial frame that wedges every clone. This is the one high-severity finding.
  - **Deadlines:** the deadline doesn't cover the write.
  - **Shutdown:** stdin can't be closed while clones exist, so shutdown always takes 2s.

`scribe:architect` is now drafting the smallest spec that makes recurrence impossible. The shape it's evaluating: a session that owns a writer task and a reader task, plus an explicit closed-with-reason state that every caller observes.

**The rest is ordinary fixes, not part of that spec:**
- **Header-size cap in the decoder:** the header can grow without bound.
- **Stderr drain:** it stops on a non-UTF-8 line and drops the pipe.
- **`handshake_timeout`:** it's never read.
- **`failed` flag:** the restart-storm flag never resets.
- **Restart replay:** a restarted request replays into a fresh session unchanged.
- **Node fallback:** on a Node without `execve`, tsc runs as a grandchild that the kill doesn't reach.

**The crate is not committed yet.** I'd hold the commit until the spec's fix lands. The alternative is to commit now as a known-defective first cut and fix it in a follow-up on a stacked PR. Tell me which you prefer once the spec is back.

questions.question: On shutdown, what happens to requests still in flight?

options.label: Fail immediately (Recommended)
options.description: In-flight requests get SessionClosed the moment shutdown starts. Deterministic, and real tsc exits on stdin EOF in about 1 ms anyway.

options.label: Let them land first
options.description: Wait up to the 2s grace period for responses before failing the rest. Friendlier to slow queries, but shutdown latency becomes unbounded by the caller's own deadlines.

questions.question: A child that always sends a bad header now burns the 3-restart budget in 3 calls. Restart on every kind of session end?

options.label: Yes, restart on any (Recommended)
options.description: Simple rule with no exceptions: a closed session is restarted, and the storm cap bounds a misbehaving child. This is what removes the never-restarts bug (NEW-1).

options.label: Not for frame errors
options.description: Treat MalformedFrame/OversizedFrame as non-restartable and return them immediately. A frame error usually means a real tsc bug or version mismatch, so restarting rarely helps, but every caller then handles a second failure mode.

questions.question: Where should the write-queue size (16 whole frames) live?

options.label: A const (Recommended)
options.description: Fixed bounded queue of 16 frames. Nothing to tune until a real consumer exists.

options.label: A SupervisorConfig field
options.description: Callers can tune it now. More API surface to keep stable before any consumer needs it.

# 0007. A session owns its child's I/O and closes once, with a reason

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-09-28

## Context

`crates/tsc-client` is the Rust client for `tsc --api` (ADR 0006). Its first cut let any caller's `request()` future write to the child's stdin under a shared mutex, and nothing recorded that a session had ended. An audit against the Lifecycle gate in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` reproduced six failures from that one cause:

- Dropping a request future mid-write left a partial frame on the pipe. Every later request on every `Client` clone timed out, and `is_alive()` stayed `true`.
- A child that stopped reading stdin blocked a write past its deadline and queued every other caller behind the mutex.
- A request made after the reader exited, or in flight during `shutdown()`, waited out its whole deadline and reported `Timeout`.
- A fatal frame error from a child that stayed alive was never restarted, because the supervisor only matched `Crashed | Write`.
- Stdin closed only when every `Client` clone dropped, so shutdown always spent the 2 s grace period and then sent SIGKILL.

Patching each one leaves the cause in place: no one owned the pipe, and no state said the session was over.

## Decision

A session owns its I/O and ends exactly once.

- **One writer.** A writer task alone holds `ChildStdin`. Callers send whole frames over a bounded channel (`WRITE_QUEUE_FRAMES = 16`), so a dropped request future has enqueued a full frame or nothing.
- **One close.** A set-once closed state carries the reason. Reader exit, a write failure and `Supervisor::shutdown` all set it. Setting it fails every pending waiter and stops the writer, which drops stdin even while `Client` clones are alive.
- **One deadline.** `request()` puts enqueue and response under a single deadline and fails at once when the session is closed.
- **Restarts follow state.** The supervisor decides restarts from the closed state only. It never matches error variants or polls task handles. Shutdown closes the session first, then reaps the child and returns its exit status.

## Consequences

- A task and a channel replace a mutex. That is the point: the mutex version is what the audit broke.
- The queue is bounded in frames, not bytes. Sixteen 8 MiB frames can hold 128 MiB.
- Any close reason triggers a restart. A child that always sends a bad header burns the three-restart budget in three calls, and the storm cap then stops it.
- A `Client` clone from before a restart fails at once with its own session's reason, not a generic error.
- Each task holds a guard that closes the session on drop, so a panicking task cannot leave a session open.
- A cancelled `Supervisor::request` can burn one restart attempt.
- Enforced by tests: `dropping_a_request_future_mid_write_never_wedges_the_session`, `a_child_that_stops_reading_stdin_cannot_hold_a_request_past_its_deadline`, `shutdown_wakes_requests_blocked_on_a_full_write_queue`, `shutdown_fails_in_flight_requests_on_clones_with_session_closed` and `a_fatal_frame_from_a_live_child_is_restarted_not_timed_out`. `ChildStdin` is moved into the writer task and sits in no struct field, so no other code can write to the pipe.

## Alternatives considered

- **Patch each instance** (a liveness check per call, a stdin timeout, abort the reader after draining). Each patch leaves the shared cause, and the next instance is one edit away.
- **Keep the mutex, add a write timeout.** A timed-out `write_all` still leaves a partial frame that desyncs tsc's decoder.
- **Unbounded queue.** Memory grows without limit against a child that stops reading.

The crate and its ADR are committed as two commits on `main`. Neither is pushed, and no PR is open.

```
84ed10f docs(adr): record why a session owns its child's I/O and closes once
1f0be33 feat(tsc-client): add the Rust client and process supervisor for tsc --api
```

- **Crate commit:** all of `crates/tsc-client` plus the workspace member and lockfile changes. It's a standalone crate that nothing consumes yet. All 45 tests pass, and fmt, clippy and `cargo deny` are clean. The smoke test round-trips against the real 7.1 nightly and shuts down in about 1 ms.
- **ADR commit:** ADR 0007 with its README index entry. It records the boundary, the six audit failures it came from, the enforcing tests and the rejected alternatives. I also updated the Lifecycle row and "Next step" in `docs/type-checker-integration.md`, which no longer says "not started".

Three files are still modified and deliberately left out: `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json` and `.github/hooks/entire.json`. Each was rewritten by tooling (the plugin reload, or the `entire` CLI), not by this work.

Lifecycle items still open, all listed in the doc:
- decoder header-size cap
- stderr that isn't UTF-8
- honoring `handshake_timeout`
- recovery after the restart cap trips
- whether a restarted request may replay

Cost hasn't been re-measured through the Rust client yet.

Per your note on `gh stack`, I can open these as a stacked PR next if you want: crate first, ADR on top.
Remember ADRs are for architectural decisions, not internal decisions, or repo config decisions right?

Yes, and ADR 0007 doesn't pass the repo's own gates. The design lives entirely inside one crate that nothing consumes yet, and it came out of a bug audit. `docs/adr/README.md` lists both of those as commit-message or code-comment material. The architect's "yes, it warrants an ADR" argued the boundary would constrain future wiring, but callers only see `Supervisor::request`, so the writer task and closed state are an implementation detail. I shouldn't have taken that verdict at face value. I'm removing the ADR and keeping the durable "why" in the crate's own docs.
